A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Quamba2 work, with readable text, equations, tables, figures and appendices. v4 retains Appendices A–F and adds Appendix G; no material reading gaps prevent comparison.

before.justification: Sections 5–6 and Appendices A–F report original quantization accuracy, generation, latency, memory and ablation results.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results and adds energy measurements for Mamba2-8B in Appendix G.

M1.justification: The sort-and-cluster method, per-state-group quantization, weight reordering, Hadamard fusion, quantized kernels and states, and mixed-precision search are unchanged. Appendix G evaluates existing configurations.

E1.justification: Pile calibration and evaluation on the six commonsense tasks, MMLU, Natural Questions and SQuAD v2 are retained. Energy profiling reuses Mamba2-8B generation on the existing A5000 and Orin Nano platforms; it adds measurements within retained task coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain Quamba, MambaQuant, the QuaRot/QServe Transformer baselines and handcrafted mixed-precision controls. Appendix G uses the existing FP16 reference and Quamba2 configurations without introducing a new competing method.

E3.justification: Appendix G adds energy profiling: joules per request on Nano with 512 input and 512 generated tokens, and A5000 profiling with 1024 input and 1024 generated tokens at batch sizes 4, 8, 16, 24, 32 and 48. Figure 14 introduces the reported metric 'tokens per Gigawatt.' Existing evaluation protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix G adds a focused analysis of energy costs across precision configurations and energy efficiency across batch sizes, supported by Table 13 and Figure 14. Existing component ablations, mixed-precision analyses and memory/latency studies are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions disclose five-run accuracy averages, a fixed calibration-sampling seed and latency averages over 100 iterations. Appendix G introduces no additional repetition counts, error bars, confidence intervals or statistical estimation procedures.

E6.justification: Existing numerical results are unchanged. New Table 13 reports 231.23 J/request for W4A8 and 225.46 J/request for W4A16 on Nano, with FP16 out of memory. Figure 14 adds A5000 efficiency results favoring Quamba2 over FP16 wherever both run; these are newly reported measurements, not improvements over v3 results.

T1.justification: The quantization and SSM definitions, Equations 1–3, Hadamard identities and fusion reasoning are retained. Appendix G adds no formal mathematical definition, derivation or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same methodological contributions, supported bit-widths and backbones, and speed, memory and accuracy claims. The energy appendix supplements their evidence without redefining the core contribution.

C2.justification: Interpretations of quantization sensitivity, state-memory bottlenecks, mixed-precision trade-offs and generalization limitations remain unchanged. Appendix G connects its new energy observations to the existing cloud/edge deployment argument without adding a substantive mechanism explanation or applicability qualification.

D1.justification: v3's CUTLASS reference explicitly specifies version 3.0.0; v4 omits this version information. Appendix C and the code/model release information otherwise remain unchanged. This is a small documentation loss, with no evidence that the software used changed.

R1.justification: The same cited works and research positioning are retained, including the discussion of Transformer and SSM quantization. Citation ordering and bibliography formatting changes do not add or remove prior work.

P1.justification: v4 adds the short Appendix G and changes citation conventions, bibliography formatting and the version stamp. The existing prose and section organization remain substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: v4 adds the energy bar chart in Figure 14 and the Nano energy table in Table 13. References and some surrounding text reflow, while existing figures and tables retain their content and designs.

improvement.justification: Appendix G modestly strengthens deployment evidence by adding energy costs and efficiency profiles beyond v3's latency and memory measurements. The benefit is limited by missing measurement details and the unclear 'tokens per Gigawatt' definition; omission of the cited CUTLASS version also slightly weakens reproducibility. The unchanged method and prior results remain intact.
